known_facts_book1: Is large and blue, sits on the top of a mushroom with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah.
Is exactly three inches high, and says so when Alice complains that three inches is a wretched height.
Opens with 'Who are you?' and returns to the same question after every digression.
Tells Alice to keep her temper.
Makes Alice recite 'You are old, Father William', and pronounces it wrong from beginning to end.
Gets down off the mushroom and crawls away, remarking as it goes: 'One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.'
Never says which side is which, leaving Alice to work it out from a round mushroom with no sides.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Interrogates her, contradicts her, makes her recite a poem she gets wrong, and finally gives her the mushroom instruction — the only practical help she receives in the book.

not_in_this_book: the Caterpillar turns into a butterfly on the page
the Caterpillar reappears later in the book

known_facts_book1: Flies into Alice's face and beats her with its wings when her neck, stretched enormously long, comes down among the treetops.
Insists Alice is a serpent, on the grounds of her long neck and her admission that she has eaten eggs.
Complains it has tried the roots of trees, banks and hedges, and that serpents are never satisfied.
Says it has not had a wink of sleep for three weeks for watching out for serpents.
Tells Alice to be off when she says she is a little girl, and goes back down into its nest.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Mistakes her for a serpent after eggs and drives her away from its nest.

not_in_this_book: the Pigeon has eggs stolen by Alice
the Pigeon appears more than once

hallucination_signals: the Pigeon's eggs are eaten by Alice

known_facts_book1: Is not a character in the story: he is the subject of the poem Alice recites to the Caterpillar, 'You are old, Father William'.
In the poem he stands on his head, turns somersaults in at the door, eats a goose bones and beak, and balances an eel on the end of his nose.
Answers a young man's four questions and ends by threatening to kick him downstairs.

known_relations_book1.Alice: None. She recites the poem about him and gets the words wrong.
known_relations_book1.Caterpillar: None. The Caterpillar asks for the recitation.

not_in_this_book: Father William speaks to any character in the story
